item.title: Obalende MTN bus park to open December, accommodate 1,000 buses — Wahab
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has said the ongoing redevelopment of the Obalende Bus Park, known as the Y’ello Bus Park, will be completed and ready for public use by the end of December 2026. The facility, being developed by MTN Nigeria as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative, is designed to accommodate more than 1,000 buses. Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, disclosed this during an inspection tour of the Obalende project and another MTN-sponsored under-bridge recreational park at Falomo, Ikoyi. Wahab, who was accompanied by key government officials, including the Special Adviser to the Governor on Transportation, Sola Giwa; Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Adekunle Akodu; General Manager of the Lagos State Parks and Gardens Agency (LASPARK), Adetoun Popoola; and Director of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, said the six-week completion window was agreed upon after consultations with stakeholders to resolve operational challenges. He explained that the project was initially scheduled for completion within 21 weeks following an inspection of the area by Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu and his deputy as part of efforts to transform the previously degraded environment into a modern transport hub. However, construction was delayed by logistical challenges involving existing transport operators conducting business at the site. Wahab said the government had engaged the transport unions, contractors and the Special Adviser on Transportation to agree on temporarily relocating operators from the immediate construction area to enable the contractors to complete the work. “Today was just to see how far they’ve gone. Thankfully, they had one or two logistics issues that had to do with the businesses that have been operating there, legacy things like the transport business. “We had to engage the Special Adviser to the Governor on Transportation, the transport unions, and the contractors to see how we can give them a space for a maximum of six weeks—not shutting the place down 100 per cent, but moving them out of that immediate workspace to enable the contractors to complete it and hand it over to them to operate,” he said. The upgraded facility is designed to accommodate approximately 1,000 buses and will feature dedicated parking and loading bays, sleeping facilities for drivers, modern toilet facilities and green areas. The design also incorporates collapsible barriers along the perimeter to allow drainage maintenance teams access to the adjoining canal for regular cleaning and maintenance. Addressing concerns about possible commercialisation of the facility and increases in transport fares, Giwa assured commuters and commercial transport operators that access to the terminal would be free. “No, there’s no toll at all. It is for them; they are the ones using it. We are just making it a standard park that we will replicate all over the state as time goes on,” he said. O

item.title: Flaws in VMware and KVM need attention, if you have time while fixing Java, PHP, and everything else
item.description: If you’ve got a moment to spare in between sorting out emergency patches for PHP , Java , and PostgreSQL , VMware has just bid for any remaining space on your schedule by publishing two critical-rated security advisories. VMSA-2026-0009 addresses CVE-2026-123890 , a 9.8-rated flaw that VMware says means a malicious actor with network access to vCenter may exploit this issue to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system. vCenter is the tool admins use to manage fleets of virtual machines. The flaw is present in VMware’s flagship Cloud Foundation suite. VMSA-2026-0009 also details four more CVEs, some of them high-severity. VMware’s second advisory, VMSA-2026-0010 , warns that Cloud Foundation, Aria Operations, and VCF Operations HCX products all use Apache – which has a 9.8-rated remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-119618). A KVM curiosity Admins who oversee virtual infrastructure also need to pay attention to Linux KVM, the subject of a curious incident over the last 24 hours. This mess started with the November 18 disclosure of CVE-2026-99312 , a bug which allows an attacker to use a guest virtual machine to inflict Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption attacks on the host. It’s bad news whenever someone with access to a guest VM can attack the host, because it means gaining access to a single tenant can potentially harm all the other guest VMs or peer into the memory a guest uses. This flaw, however, isn’t a worst-case scenario guest-host escape, because it only impacts users of AMD processors who employ nested virtualization – the practice of running a hypervisor inside a virtual machine. Nested virtualization isn’t commonly used in the enterprise, but clouds employ it to do things like powering OS emulators. The bug’s CVSSv3 score is therefore a modest 5.5. Security researcher Oren Tomtov of Accomplish.ai says the flaw meant he could access 127 GB of host RAM on a Digital Ocean “Droplet” – the junior cloud’s name for its cloudy VMs. Yomtov says he told Digital Ocean and the Linux kernel security team about the flaw in October. Maintainers got busy and delivered a fix to the mainline kernel on November 2, full fixes landed on the 17 th . The CVE then appeared on November 18. Yomtov and Terra Security quickly posted their analysis of the flaw – but then took the posts down within hours. The Register understands that Digital Ocean asked for the posts to come down because it needed more time to update its Linux implementations. The company has not responded to multiple requests for comment. Terra’s analysis of the flaw asserts that it was introduced to KVM in 2022, when developers wrote a fix for CVE-2022-3344 . The company believes 3.2 percent of CVEs in the Linux kernel were introduced by the fix for another CVE. The good news about CVE-2026-99312 is it’s easy to defeat without an update, by disabling nested virtualization in KVM. ®

item.title: UNIZIK VC urges 19,522 graduands to uphold discipline, excellence
item.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA – The Vice-Chancellor of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, Prof. Ugochukwu Bond Stanley Anyaehie, has urged the 2025 and 2026 graduating students of the institution to uphold its core values of discipline, excellence and self-reliance as they begin the next phase of their lives. Anyaehie gave the charge on Thursday in Awka while delivering his address at the university’s 20th and 21st combined convocation ceremonies. He urged the graduands to become worthy ambassadors of the institution, named after Nigeria’s first President, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, popularly known as Zik of Africa. Expounding on the university’s motto, the Vice-Chancellor said discipline required the graduands to make integrity, self-control and ethical conduct their guiding principles in an increasingly complex world. On self-reliance, he advised them not to wait for opportunities to come their way but to embrace innovation, create value, build enterprises and develop solutions to real-life challenges. He also urged them to pursue excellence and reject mediocrity, stressing that every task they undertook should reflect world-class standards. Reflecting on his tenure as the institution’s seventh Vice-Chancellor, Anyaehie reaffirmed his commitment to scholarship, clinical integrity, effective higher education governance, staff development and institutional transformation. He said his administration’s philosophy, “A Greater UNIZIK is Possible,” was not merely a slogan but a commitment to repositioning the university as a globally competitive centre of academic excellence, technological innovation and societal impact. Presenting the convocation statistics, the Vice-Chancellor disclosed that a total of 19,522 graduands would receive various qualifications, comprising 16,260 first-degree recipients and 3,262 postgraduate graduands. Of the first-degree recipients, 213 graduated with First Class Honours, 4,623 obtained Second Class Honours (Upper Division), 8,751 earned Second Class Honours (Lower Division), while 2,116 graduated with Third Class Honours and 71 obtained Pass degrees. Another 486 students received unclassified degrees in Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences. The postgraduate category comprised 701 Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) recipients, 35 Master of Philosophy/Doctor of Philosophy (MPhil/PhD) recipients, 1,224 master’s degree recipients, 323 Postgraduate Diploma (PGD) recipients and 979 Postgraduate Diploma in Education (PGDE-NTI) recipients. Highlighting his administration’s achievements, Anyaehie said institutional reforms had been implemented to strengthen academic standards, improve staff welfare, expand the university’s capacity and modernise its operations. He also identified the full re-accreditation of the university’s Medical programme by the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) as a major milestone in its academic and professional development. item.title: Ogun polytechnic students protest ASUP strike, seek Abiodun’s intervention
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — Students of state-owned polytechnics in Ogun State on Thursday protested at the Governor’s Office, Oke Mosan, Abeokuta, demanding Governor Dapo Abiodun’s urgent intervention to end the lingering industrial dispute between the state government and the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP). The protest, organised by hundreds of students under the aegis of the National Association of Polytechnic Students (NAPS), followed the expiration of two separate 48-hour ultimatums issued to the government without what the students described as concrete action towards resolving the dispute. The strike, which has kept students out of classrooms for about 10 days, has disrupted academic activities across the six state-owned polytechnics. Armed with placards bearing inscriptions such as “Gov. Dapo Abiodun, please end ASUP strike”, “Save Polytechnic Education Now”, “Our Lecturers Must Return to the Classroom” and “Attend to Our Lecturers’ Demands”, the protesters urged the governor to intervene personally and ensure an immediate resolution of the crisis. Speaking during the demonstration, the Chairman of NAPS, Ogun State Liaison Council, Comrade Joshua Opatunmibi, said the students had exhausted available diplomatic channels and could no longer remain silent while their academic future was being jeopardised. He explained that the protest was not intended to confront the state government but to draw attention to the hardship caused by the prolonged strike and demand decisive action. Opatunmibi said the students had made several appeals to the government and issued two 48-hour ultimatums without the desired response. He said: “On November 12, we issued a 48-hour ultimatum to the state government, appealing to Governor Dapo Abiodun to urgently intervene and bring an end to the ongoing ASUP strike. “The 48 hours elapsed without any meaningful action from the government. Consequently, on Monday, we addressed another press conference, appealing to the government to come to our rescue because the strike had stalled our education. We also issued another 48-hour ultimatum. “That ultimatum expired on Wednesday afternoon, but we were disappointed that nothing had been done to address our concerns. We are really unhappy. Does it mean that the government does not care about our plight? “The closure of all the polytechnics in the state is seriously affecting us. We cannot continue to sit at home while our academic programmes and future plans are being put on hold. “We are here to demonstrate that the voices of students matter. We are not fighting the government; we are simply demanding that the issues responsible for this strike be resolved. “We cannot continue to put our future in jeopardy. We appeal to Governor Abiodun to please attend to the demands of our lecturers so that we can return to our respective institutions and complete our education.” Also speaking, a NAPS member, Kolade Musbau, expressed disappointment over what he de

item.title: Germ Network infects Android, but in a good way
item.description: The Germ Network encrypted messaging client, known as Germ DM, became available for Android on Wednesday, and made a bigger splash than its iOS touchdown back in 2023. "Our usage took a 20x jump yesterday from our Android launch ," co-founder Tessa Brown, a communications scholar and former Stanford lecturer, told The Register in an interview. "Android has been really exciting for us because not only is it 70 percent of the global mobile market, but we rolled out on iOS first. People were so excited to use Germ for their end-to-end encrypted Bluesky DMs, but half of their friends couldn't talk to them." Building a new messaging platform isn't easy, much less one with credible end-to-end encryption. Co-founder Mark Xue hails from Apple, where he worked as a privacy engineer on systems like iMessage and FaceTime. "At the core level, the end-to-end encryption is built on a standardized encryption and Messaging Layer Security," Xue said. "The premise of Messaging Layer Security was to be as good as Signal and deployable by many, many different parties in different applications, which we're taking advantage of to extend the reach of that encryption." Xue said the app is built with its own transport protocol to minimize the amount of message metadata, adding that while the team hasn't gotten around to a formal security audit, it's a step they're considering. Germ Network's goal, said Brown, is to give people more confidence when they communicate. "We do that by giving you more tools to protect your identity, to control what you're sharing with whom," she explained. Instead of using a person's phone number as an identity key, Germ allows users to create cards which represent distinct identities on the network. "Instead of sharing your number, you share a card," Brown explained. "You can build multiple cards; they're not mutually discoverable. And our vision for the product that will continue shipping over the coming years is that these cards become a more intelligent way to manage your social life, even your work life." At some point, AI might play a role in that, but both Xue and Brown expressed reservations about the current state of play. Citing concerns Signal has raised about the integration of AI and messaging, Xue said, "The products today that I might characterize as technology demos, they're most powerful when they run on someone else's computer. So you end up with these systems where you upload all your messages or you give another entity the power to observe your computing, and that's extremely dangerous for what we protect as private content." Xue noted rapid progress toward addressing information exposure concerns and therefore plans to explore the kinds of smart tooling that users want while also meeting security and privacy requirements. "I think a lot of the AI conversation sometimes is a hammer in search of a nail," said Brown. item.title: Only 20% of Nigeria’s 30,000 PHCs functional, family physicians raise alarm
item.description: By Matthew Johnson The Society of Family Physicians of Nigeria, SOFPON, yesterday raised the alarm over the state of primary healthcare in the country, revealing that only about 20 per cent of more than 30,000 Primary Healthcare Centres ,PHCs, nationwide are fully functional. Vice-President of SOFPON, Dr Ibrahim Yakubu, who disclosed this during a press conference themed, “Primary Health Care Without Family Physicians: Can Nigeria Afford the Gap?”, will also focus on “The Double Burden of Disease and the Cost of Fragmented Care” and “The Stressed Family Physician and Continuity of Care”. on November 19th 2026 ahead of the society’s 29th Annual General and Scientific Meeting ,AGSM, said the country’s primary healthcare system was facing a serious operational crisis. He explained that the shortage of skilled medical personnel, poor funding and increasing migration of doctors were undermining access to quality healthcare, calling on the Federal Government and state governors to urgently integrate family physicians into the leadership of primary healthcare facilities. Yakubu who said the majority of PHCs were unable to provide essential medical services due to structural decay, inadequate funding and shortage of skilled health professionals. According to him, the conference will develop policy and clinical recommendations on integrating specialist services into primary healthcare, improving physician welfare and retention, and developing integrated care models for infectious and chronic diseases. He described the situation was being worsened by the increasing migration of doctors, particularly frontline medical professionals, due to poor working conditions, inadequate equipment and weak welfare structures. He said loss or sidelining of family physicians could further weaken the country’s healthcare delivery system, particularly at the grassroots where continuous and comprehensive medical care is required. He further explained that family physicians were specially trained to manage patients holistically, coordinate treatment and address both infectious and chronic diseases at the primary healthcare level. Yakubu said the country’s healthcare system was battling a double burden of disease, with communicable illnesses such as malaria, tuberculosis and cholera existing alongside rising cases of non-communicable diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, kidney diseases and cancer. He warned that the absence of coordinated healthcare services was increasing treatment costs for families and making it difficult to manage patients with multiple health conditions. He said the society also urged governments to move beyond constructing PHC buildings to adequately equipping existing facilities and providing sufficient funding and personnel to operate them. Yakubu added that positioning family physicians at the centre of primary healthcare would promote early detection of chronic illnesses, reduce treatment costs and ensure continuity of care. item.title: Voyager 1 team, unbowed by communications glitch, celebrates epic 1-light-day distance milestone
item.description: null PASADENA, Calif. – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov. 19), celebrating a big milestone — Voyager 1 just reached one light-day from Earth , something no other spacecraft has ever done. The excitement persisted despite a communication anomaly that cropped up on the probe, which the team remains confident is temporary. Voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2 , flew past Neptune. The gathering served to celebrate Voyager 1 's distance milestone: At 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 18), the probe reached one light-day from Earth — the distance a photon travels in one day, which is about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). That means it now takes a full day for a signal to travel from Earth to Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object out in space. "I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day. What an incredible milestone," Voyager project scientist Linda Spilker said during Thursday's event. An unexpected, but manageable, anomaly While this day and this week have been chock-full of excitement over the distance milestone, the Voyager mission team has been hard at work, as usual, keeping the two nearly 50-year-old spacecraft alive and functioning. Unfortunately, as JPL spokesperson Raquel Villanueva shared at this celebration, on Saturday (Nov. 14), Voyager 1 stopped transmitting science and engineering data. The team has remained in contact with Voyager 1 while investigating the issue, and they are confident that they'll be able to solve it soon. NASA and Voyager team members celebrate Voyager 1's light-day milestone at NASA JPL on Nov. 19, 2026. From left to right: Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate; Jonathan Lunine, chief scientist, NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory; Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager; Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager; Jamie Rankin, Voyager deputy project scientist. (Image credit: Chelsea Gohd) "We listen to each spacecraft every day," Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd told Space.com at the event. Regarding Voyager 1, "we have an anomaly that is not something unseen before," Dodd said. "We do have a very strong carrier signal. We currently don't have a frame sync, so we're not getting the science or engineering data currently." "But if you recall," Dodd added, "one light-day is very far from us. [It takes] 24 hours to get the signal to the spacecraft, 24 hours for the signal to come down, so it takes two days to diagnose anything on the spacecraft … So we can't do anything fast, and the data rates are very low." According to Dodd, this anomaly isn't a major cause for long-term concern. Rather, it's likely just part of the na

item.title: Afreximbank provides $30 m to finance Nigerian SME exports through NEXIM
item.description: Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) is to finance export-oriented Nigerian Small and Medium -sized Enterprises (SMEs). The Regional bank announced that the facility would be provided through the Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM). “The facility will finance working capital and capital expenditure for export and intra-African trade activities, with eligible businesses in fashion, film, music, design and the wider creative industries among the intended beneficiaries,” Afreximbank said in a statement issued toay. The facility reinforces Afreximbank’s broader commitment to expanding access to finance for African SMEs and exporters, including eligible businesses in the creative economy, the institution said. It said the agreement was signed on behalf of Afreximbank by Mrs. Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice President, Intra-African Trade and Export Development, and on behalf of NEXIM by Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer , at the recent CANEX event in Lagos. “Nigeria’s SMEs and export-oriented businesses need access to finance to expand production, invest in productive capacity and compete in new markets. This US$30 million facility will enable NEXIM to provide the working capital and investment financing required to support their growth and increase Nigeria’s exports across Africa and beyond,” Mrs. Awani was quoted as saying. “By combining NEXIM’s export-finance capabilities with Afreximbank’s trade and development mandate, we can help more Nigerian enterprises build the capacity required to participate in regional and global value chains. Eligible creative businesses will also be able to benefit from the facility, supporting CANEX’s broader objective of connecting African talent and enterprise with appropriate finance and market opportunities,” she added. Welcoming the partnership, Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NEXIM said, “We are delighted to partner with Afreximbank to expand financing opportunities for Nigerian exporters. This US$30 million facility marks an important step in our efforts to help more businesses add value locally, fulfil export orders and reach new markets across Africa and beyond. SMEs operating across the export value chain, including eligible businesses in the creative industries, will also be able to access financing through this facility. We are particularly pleased that this partnership will help more Nigerian businesses strengthen their capacity to compete in regional and global markets, supporting our country’s economic diversification.” The Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) is Afreximbank’s flagship programme for Africa’s creative and cultural industries. It supports the development of commercially sustainable, export-ready creative businesses through access to finance, skills, markets, commercial partnerships and policy support. CANEX WKND 2026 took place from 5 to 8 November at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Cultural & Creative Arts

item.title: Africa must be co-investor, not aid recipient, in proposed GECF gas bank — Expert
item.description: By Nkiruka Nnorom African countries must enter the proposed Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) gas bank as co-investors and strategic partners, rather than mere aid recipients, an energy policy expert has said. Energy policy, markets and regulation consultant, Ifey Ikoneu, made the call at the conclusion of the Eighth Summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow, while assessing key directions of Russian-African energy cooperation. Assessing the initiative to create a gas bank, Ikoneu described it as very good, but warned that its success would depend directly on a balance of interests. “It is important that this does not become just another multilateral investment institution where Africa’s interests are not put first,” she said. According to her, African countries should act not merely as recipients of funds, but as co-investors and full participants in strategic decision-making. Ikoneu said the bank should not only finance export infrastructure, but also the continent’s domestic needs, including electrification, petrochemicals, fertilizer production and industrial development, even given that many such projects are traditionally considered non-bankable. For the new structure to work effectively, she said it would need transparency, protection from political interference and coordination with the African Development Bank, Afreximbank and Africa Finance Corporation. She stressed that the continent’s domestic needs are extremely acute despite its wealth of energy resources with more than 600 million people in sub-Saharan Africa living without access to electricity. In this context, she said the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline — a project long stalled due to financing problems — takes on particular significance. Ikoenu noted that launching it requires a strong institutional framework among Nigeria, Niger and Algeria. At the same time, the pipeline should serve not only as an export channel to Europe but also as a driver of industrialisation for the participating countries. This, according to her, applies especially to Niger, which is critically dependent on imported electricity and costly diesel generators. An infrastructure union, she said, will allow the three countries to collectively defend their interests on the export market, while giving Russia the opportunity to act as a strategic partner both in the construction itself and in training the necessary personnel. Touching on the principle of technological neutrality enshrined in the GECF Moscow Declaration, the expert called for interpreting it as broadly as possible. “This should mean not just a choice between imported technologies, but also the freedom to develop one’s own,” she said. Ikoneu proposed creating a joint Russian-African research and innovation centre in the gas sector, expanding scholarship programmes for African students in Russia, and more actively involving women in the energy sector. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 19, 2005: Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft makes 1st-ever liftoff from surface of an asteroid
item.description: null On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Hayabusa was supposed to return asteroid samples to Earth. Asteroids are space rocks that were formed during the early solar system. We study asteroids to learn more about the solar system's history. Hayabusa (pronounced HI-uh-BOOS-uh) made two touchdowns on asteroid Itokawa (EE -toh-KA-wah). Each time, the spacecraft went into safe mode. Controllers weren't sure if Hayabusa gathered any material. But they sent the spacecraft back to Earth anyway. Hayabusa's sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010 . Scientists found dust of Itokawa inside the capsule, proving that it did indeed capture samples of Itokawa. An artist's illustration of Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft landing on asteroid Itokawa. (Image credit: JAXA) Why it mattered The primary goal of Japan's Hayabusa mission to asteroid Itokawa was never to be the first spacecraft to liftoff from a space rock. The mission was always aimed at collecting samples from an asteroid and returning them to Earth. It was a hard road to Itokawa for Hayabusa. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) launched the probe on May 9, 2003, with plans for an arrival at the asteroid in the early summer of 2005. That asteroid arrival was delayed until September 2005 after a solar storm degraded Hayabusa's solar arrays, limiting the available power for its ion engines. The asteroid Itokawa as seen by Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft. (Image credit: JAXA) Still, Hayabusa managed to limp along its path to reach the asteroid Itokawa on Sept. 12, 2005. Hayabusa dropped a small lander onto Itokawa, but that probe was apparently lost. Hayabusa then dropped a landing target on the asteroid, and ultimately managed to touchdown about 99 feet from the marker, JAXA has said. During its first landing on Nov. 19, Hayabusa descended to a point just 56 feet above Itokawa before going silent for 3 hours, according to an Associated Press report . Once contact was restored, JAXA officials confirmed the probe had landed, and it eventually lifted off for a second attempt. That was the first-ever liftoff from an asteroid by a spacecraft. "The spacecraft actually bounced off the surface a few times and spent about 39 minutes resting on the asteroid, but apparently the samplers never fired," Andrew Cheng, a Hayabusa science team member at Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory, told Space.com at the time . There was hope that some material managed to make it inside the collector anyway. "After all the thrashing about ... there is no way to confirm that," Cheng had said. The second landing on Itokawa occured a few days later on Nov. 26, 2005. In November 2010, five months after Hayabusa's sample-return capsule touched down in Australia, JAXA announced some good news: Hayabusa did collect 1,500 dust grains from asteroid Itokawa, samples that were jammed into the collector by the two landings, despite is collector mechanism not

item.title: Inside Bukele’s Casa Presidencial Dinner: Bitcoiners Discuss Energy, Immigration, and El Salvador’s Future
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Inside Bukele’s Casa Presidencial Dinner: Bitcoiners Discuss Energy, Immigration, and El Salvador’s Future This November 10, in the midst of the Bitcoin Histórico conference taking place in the Historical Center of San Salvador, a group of Bitcoiners representing a wide range of sectors within the industry met with President Bukele. The dinner was organized by The Bitcoin Office, which is part of the Office of the President, and was led by Stacy Herbert and Max Keiser. The dinner went on from about 7:30 pm to 10:30 pm local time and included about thirty Bitcoiners, many regular visitors to El Salvador. Photograph by the Bitcoin Office. Among the guests was billionaire Ricardo Salinas Pliego, founder of Grupo Salinas, which owns Banco Azteca. Salinas is a known Bitcoiner, who has made public appearances with Keiser and Herbert in the past, and is speculated to be planning a run at the next Mexican Presidential election. Salinas met privately with the President besides the dinner and reportedly gifted him volumes one and two of Manuscripts of the Conquistadors, works curated and edited by Jorge Nikaido, Chief of Staff of Grupo Salinas. Representing investors and founders were Parker Lewis, founder of Unchained Capital, Mike Peterson of Bitcoin Beach fame, Katie Ananina of Citizen X, and Aleks Svetski, entrepreneur and founder of Satlantis. Bitcoin miners also attended, such as Beau Turner, CEO of Abundant Mines, Nacho Pauls, CCO of OCEAN Mining, and Adam Ortolf of Denver Bitcoin mining. Jon Atack, a Bitcoin core contributor, was also at the dinner alongside engineer Giacomo Zucco of Plan B Network, and AI tech entrepreneurs Ginger Gaetz of the ANIA AI initiative and Marc Seal, Founder of Aevonix. The academic and media side of the industry was also heavily represented, with none other than Michael Goldstein, also known as Bitstein and co-founder of the Nakamoto Institute. Eric Yakes, economist and author of The 7th Property , was there, as well as Efrat Feningson, independent journalist and podcaster. Local Bitcoiner Michael Ruiz also attended the dinner; he is the founder of Build in El Salvador (BIS), an increasingly popular kind of business club and Bitcoin meetup mix. Setting the Table Photograph by the Bitcoin Office. The guests arrived at the Casa Presidencial earlier in the evening and were chatting and networking while waiting for the president. Max Keiser, always a showman, arrived at the Casa Presidencial with a gift some might speculate carried a magical artefact. Photographed above, the case was said to contain a Stetson El Presidente cowboy hat, though some have speculated it might in fact have carried the Philosopher’s Stone. Upon arrival, Bukele shook everyone’s hand and quickly invited them to take their assigned seats, dine, and relax- no big speeches or over-the-top formalities, Ananina told Bitcoin Magazine, describing the dinner as a kind of open mic. “President Bukele’s table was adorned with bitcoin orange fl

item.title: The view from the tower: Watch Starship come in for chopsticks catch in epic slo-mo video
item.description: null A new set of slo-mo videos gives us a new perspective on SpaceX's first-ever recovery of a Starship upper stage. The company notched the milestone on Saturday (Nov. 14), when the launch tower at its Starbase site in South Texas caught Starship's Ship spacecraft with its "chopstick" arms. You've probably seen photos and videos showing the epic snag from afar. But on Tuesday (Nov. 17), SpaceX released up-close views — a series of four slo-mo videos captured by cameras near the top of the 480-foot-tall (146 meters) tower. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) "The Starbase tower chopsticks catching their first Starship. This unique architecture was designed for full and rapid reusability, enabling repeat launches and landings from the same pad," SpaceX wrote in a Tuesday X post that shared the videos, a compilation of which you can see embedded above. Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built. Its current "V3" version stands about 408 feet (124 m) tall, and future iterations will be even larger . As SpaceX noted in Tuesday's post, the megarocket is also designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first for an orbital launch system. The company plans to catch both Starship stages — Ship and the Super Heavy booster — at the launch tower, a recovery strategy designed to enable efficient inspection, refurbishment and reflight. Another view of the chopsticks catch on Nov. 14. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX planned to carry out such a double catch on this most recent test flight , Starship's 15th to date, which launched on Friday evening (Nov. 13). But Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel warning during its return to Starbase about 6.5 minutes after launch and autonomously diverted to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico. That wasn't a huge deal for SpaceX, as it had already caught Super Heavy on three previous test flights . Snagging Ship is tougher; the upper stage returns to Earth from orbit, so it comes in faster and hotter than the booster does. SpaceX had not even attempted a Ship catch before Flight 15. But the company managed to pull off the maneuver on its first try. And Ship did some work in orbit before coming home: It deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites on Flight 15, the second batch that the company has sent to low Earth orbit . The first set was deployed on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28.

item.title: ‘Obi Will Disgrace Him Spectacularly In Anambra,’ Momodu Dismisses Soludo’s Victory Promise For Tinubu
item.description: A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Dele Momodu, has dismissed Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s prediction that President Bola Tinubu will win the 2027 presidential election, insisting that Peter Obi will defeat the President in the state. Momodu, the Deputy Director-General of Media and Communications of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, said Obi would defeat Soludo “spectacularly” during the election. “With due respect to Prof. (Soludo), he has joined those people I said were speaking like robots about Tinubu. “I guarantee you that Peter Obi will disgrace him spectacularly during the election,” he said. The former Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) presidential aspirant made the remarks on Thursday while appearing on Channels Television’s Politics Today . Asked whether Obi could win Anambra despite Soludo and former governor Chris Ngige supporting Tinubu, and whether he had seen the crowd at the APC rally in the state, Momodu dismissed the significance of the gathering. “It’s good to see the crowd, but I am telling you they are beginning to nauseate Nigerians, and that is why Nigerians are shouting ‘bamayi, bamayi’,” he said. He also claimed that criticism of Tinubu was growing, with leaders increasingly expressing their dissatisfaction with the president. On the APC’s campaign activities across the country, Momodu argued that the ruling party’s extensive mobilisation reflected its concerns about the outcome of the election. “The only reason they are going everywhere feverishly is because they know they will lose the election. I am 66-plus. I have never seen this kind of campaign where the President is beginning to sound like an opposition leader,” he said. Momodu also accused Tinubu of treating APC governors like “robots,” alleging that their public statements appeared coordinated. “I monitored each of the governors. Let me tell you emphatically that they are being treated like robots. There is no question about it,” he said. ﻿ Soludo had earlier on Thursday declared that Tinubu did not need to rig the 2027 election because his administration’s performance would secure his re-election. “To our people, this election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The President doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig the election. “All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shetima’s ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others,” he said at an APC presidential campaign rally in Anambra State attended by top party chieftains. This combined photo shows Peter Obi (L); Bola Tinubu (C); and Atiku Abubakar (R) Peter Obi, who contested the 2023 presidential election on the platform of the Labour Party, won Anambra State and finished third nationally with more than six million votes. item.title: Strategy (MSTR) Shares Tumble for Sixth Straight Day to $86 as Bitcoin Slides
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategy (MSTR) Shares Tumble for Sixth Straight Day to $86 as Bitcoin Slides Strategy (MSTR) shares fell 4.6% on Thursday to close at $86.13, their sixth straight daily decline, as bitcoin dipped below $62,000 and a broad selloff hit U.S. stocks. In after hours trading, shares were down to $85.50. The stock opened near $93 and slid through the afternoon, finishing near its low of about $86. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped more than 1,000 points, and the Nasdaq Composite lost about 2.1%. Bitcoin touched a low of $61,658 during the session, its weakest price since July. It was back near $62,000 late in the afternoon. Strategy stock extends its slide The drop adds to a brutal month for the largest corporate holder of bitcoin. Strategy shares are down about 37% from their $136.02 close on Oct. 19, and down about 29% from the $121.07 close on Nov. 10, which is when the latest leg lower began. Thursday was the stock’s sixth consecutive losing session. The slide has wiped out most of the year’s value. Strategy closed 2025 at $151.95, which puts the stock down about 43% in 2026. The shares fell below $100 on Tuesday and now trade about 11% below Tuesday’s $96.50 close. That day they also dipped under the company’s STRC preferred for the first time since mid-August. Thursday’s move tracked bitcoin closely. Institutions have kept buying even so, and a New York state pension fund boosted its stake by more than 10% in a recent filing. The bitcoin price slumped under $62,000 as traders weighed the risk of Federal Reserve rate hikes and a sharp pullback in technology stocks. Holdings now sit well below cost Strategy added 485 bitcoin in the week ending Nov. 15, according to its Nov. 16 Form 8-K. It paid $33.4 million, or an average of $68,887 per coin, and its total reached 850,849 BTC. Those coins cost $64.20 billion, or an average of $75,452 each. With bitcoin near $62,000, the stack is worth roughly $52.8 billion, which leaves Strategy with an unrealized loss of about $11 billion. Bitcoin is trading about 18% below the company’s average purchase price. The 850,849 coins are more than 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap, and the company also held about $4.9 billion in U.S. dollar reserves as of Nov. 15, which gives it a cushion for preferred dividends and buybacks. Strategy has not announced a new purchase since that filing. It has reported its buys on Mondays in recent weeks, so the next update would normally come Monday. Preferred buybacks take priority Most of Strategy’s recent cash has gone to its preferred stock instead of bitcoin. In the same filing, the company said it repurchased 2,282,510 shares of its STRC preferred for $228.1 million, nearly seven times what it spent on bitcoin. It funded the purchases with $244.7 million raised from selling common stock. The 8-K shows $332.2 million remaining under the preferred repurchase program and $1.0 billion under its common stock buyback authorization. Executive Chairman Michae

item.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Charges Eight Colorado Firms in $37 Million Fake Crypto Platform Scam The SEC charged eight Colorado-based entities on Thursday with running a fake investment adviser and crypto trading platform scheme that took more than $37 million from U.S. investors. The agency said the defendants are likely operated by people overseas. According to the SEC’s complaint , filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, the defendants defrauded more than 1,500 investors from at least August 2024 through May 2026. The advisers and the trading platforms they pointed victims to were fronts, the agency alleged, and none of the crypto assets investors thought they were buying existed. How the scheme worked Social media ads sent prospective victims to WhatsApp group and private chats run by the scammers. People in those chats posing as investment advisers first gave advice on trading U.S. stocks, then pushed victims to send as much money as possible to a supposed crypto trading platform. The complaint says the scheme ran in four adviser and platform pairs, each active for roughly six months. Advisor WeChat Capital and Tech Brokerage Asset Alliance operated from about August to December 2024. HB Wealth Advisors and IdeaCrypto Exchange followed from January to July 2025. Convergent Wealth Advisors and RealSimple Crypto Exchange ran from about July to December 2025. Associated Wealth Advisors and Essential Crypto Exchange closed out the scheme from January to May 2026. Each pair vanished after collecting millions, the SEC said, and a new one took its place. Victims were told to buy ether, tether or USDC on a U.S. exchange and move it to a self-custody wallet. They then sent it to an address supplied by the adviser, and a realistic app showed balances and gains that were invented. When investors tried to withdraw their supposed profits, they were told they first had to pay a fee, calculated as a percentage of those profits, in crypto to a separate address. The complaint says investors who balked were threatened and pressured. Eventually the websites went down and the chats went silent. Fake certificates and real losses To look legitimate, the defendants made fake SEC certificates and pointed skeptical investors to real filings with the SEC, FINRA and FinCEN. The complaint says those filings carry no regulatory approval, since registering for access to its EDGAR system is ministerial and Forms ADV are not reviewed before publication. The complaint says Convergent Wealth and Essential Crypto also filed false Forms ADV listing regulatory contacts who do not appear to be real and offices in Colorado that did not exist. The SEC said a Form D and the two Forms ADV have been removed from its website. Three unnamed investors illustrate the damage. One lost nearly $500,000, including money borrowed from a 401(k), a son and a neighbor. Another lost about $850,000, partly by liquidating a 401(k), and a third lost close to $1.6 million, including

item.title: MAHA PAC spent more on steak, luxury club than candidates, report shows
item.description: In the wake of the Make America Healthy Again movement's midterm wipeout , a top leader suggested the heavy losses came down to being outspent by wealthier, more powerful rivals. But a Stat report on MAHA's own spending in the run-up to the election raises questions about whether the group's priority was ever winning elections in the first place. The dive into the financial documents reveals that the MAHA PAC, led by Tony Lyons, spent more on allies, boosters, meals, luxuries, and its affiliated nonprofit than it did on political candidates. The findings are in stark contrast to an announcement from Lyons in the spring that he was heading a $100 million fundraiser to boost MAHA's clout in the midterms . In reality, MAHA PAC took in $3.2 million. During the election cycle, the PAC spent more than $10.5 million, with over $7 million coming from money it had collected previously. item.title: 2027: PDP insists on coalition to challenge Nwifuru in Ebonyi
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki ABAKALIKI — The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ebonyi State has insisted that a coalition of political parties and interest groups exists to challenge the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led government of Governor Francis Nwifuru in the 2027 governorship election. The party said the APC’s claim that it was not part of any coalition did not invalidate the existence of political groups working together to challenge the incumbent administration. The media aide to the PDP governorship candidate, Dr Ifeanyichukwu Odii, Dr Jerry Uhuo, stated this while reacting to comments by the APC campaign spokesman, Senator Emmanuel Onwe, who had alleged that no coalition existed in Ebonyi State. Uhuo accused Onwe of misunderstanding the concept of political coalition, explaining that it involved political interest groups coming together to pursue common objectives, including electoral victory. “From all indications, Sen. Onwe appears not to understand what coalition means in the context of the current political engineering. “Coalition is a coming together of political interest groups to work together for the interest of promoting a common interest and winning election. “The fact that the Ebonyi APC claims non-membership of such a coalition does not mean that the coalition does not exist in Ebonyi. He admitted that any group could come together to form a coalition. That alone contradicts his original position,” he said. Uhuo argued that the formation of a political coalition did not require the endorsement of a state government, insisting that political parties and interest groups were free to collaborate. He added that the PDP and other political groups were already working together to challenge the APC-led administration in the state ahead of the 2027 elections. “In the case of Ebonyi, the PDP and other political groups are already working together to dislodge the government of Governor Francis Nwifuru,” he stated. The post 2027: PDP insists on coalition to challenge Nwifuru in Ebonyi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Chase, Visa, Mastercard confirm third-party cyberattacks that may have exposed customers' info
item.description: JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard have all confirmed that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information after a data-theft-and-extortion gang claimed to have compromised the financial giants. “Visa is aware of these claims,” a spokesperson told The Register on Thursday . “They are associated with an incident involving a third-party service provider in Asia Pacific. Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. No payments data such as card numbers were affected. This is unrelated to any of the system disruptions across different industries this past week.” Mastercard also cited a third-party provider in an email sent to The Register following our questions about the alleged breach. “We were recently informed of an incident at a third-party provider that resulted in the exposure of a limited amount of email addresses - non-payments information - from a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program,” Mastercard SVP Seth Eisen said. “There is no impact to the Mastercard payment network or the ability for people to use their cards. At this time, the exposure has been contained and our teams are working with the provider to support the impacted cardholders as needed.” JPMorgan Chase did not respond to The Register ’s request for comment, but confirmed it was investigating a cyberattack on social media. “We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack,” America’s largest bank posted on X. “Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses.” According to Chase, the third-party breach didn’t disrupt any of its services, and it’s not connected to the outages earlier in the week attributed to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems. “There is no connection to service disruption some customers experienced earlier this week,” the bank said on Thursday. None of the three financial firms would comment on who the third-party providers are, when the breaches occurred, and what specific data was stolen. The Register will update this story as we learn more details about the intrusions. Extortion crew n0n claimed responsibility for all three alleged hacks, posting the financial giants to its data-leak site on Monday. The group, believed to be based in Russia, emerged in September and posted 108 victims over its first month in operations. ®

item.title: Bitcoin Price Slumps Under $62,000, Crashing 25% in One Month
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slumps Under $62,000, Crashing 25% in One Month The bitcoin price slumped under $62,000 on Thursday afternoon, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, extending a slide of about 24% in one month as Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut set off a broad selloff in tech stocks. Bitcoin was trading near $81,800 on Oct. 19. It touched a low of about $61,650 on Thursday, its weakest level since July, before steadying near $62,200. The drop was about 25% from the Oct. 19 close, based on daily data. The slide came in steps. Bitcoin closed near $80,050 on Oct. 25, about $78,250 on Nov. 1 and about $74,750 on Nov. 8. The steepest leg came last week, when it fell about 12.6% to a Nov. 15 close near $65,300, and the losses have continued this week. Bitcoin had climbed back to about $64,000 early Thursday as Anthropic’s record IPO lifted stock futures, as this morning’s report showed. The rally faded once U.S. markets opened. The bitcoin price fell from roughly $63,900 at the opening bell to about $62,200 by midday. Anthropic debut sparks a tech selloff Anthropic shares opened shortly before noon at $111.50, 34% above the $83 IPO price, CNBC reported. The opening trade valued the Claude maker at more than $2 trillion. The stock quickly pulled back and was last near $97, about 17% above its offering price. The broader market went the other way. The major averages fell to session lows soon after Anthropic began trading, as investors took profits on the AI trade. The Nasdaq Composite dropped about 2% after gaining as much as 2% earlier in the session, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost about 1,000 points. Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, told CNBC the premarket rally had faded even before Anthropic began trading. He called it the latest round of “sell the rally” trading. Nvidia (NVDA) fell about 3%, and the S&P 500 headed toward a sixth straight loss, the AP reported. The Cboe Volatility Index, Wall Street’s fear gauge, climbed to about 28 after touching nearly 29 shortly after Anthropic began trading. That was its highest level since March, up from about 24.6 at Wednesday’s close. The bitcoin price moved in step with the Nasdaq through the afternoon. Crypto stocks erase their morning gains Crypto stocks followed the Nasdaq lower in late-afternoon trading, about 3:55 p.m. ET. Strategy (MSTR) traded near $86.70, down about 4% on the day. Galaxy Digital (GLXY) dropped about 6.9%, the steepest decline in the group. Coinbase (COIN) slipped about 0.9% to near $109.50, while Circle (CRCL) fell about 2.2%. Bitcoin miners gave back their early rally too. IREN (IREN) fell about 5.6%, CleanSpark (CLSK) lost about 5.4% and MARA Holdings (MARA) declined about 4.2%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) was down about 2.9%. Fed hike risk keeps pressure on the bitcoin price The Fed remains a headwind. item.title: 14 killed as truck carrying passengers, cattle crashes in Niger
item.description: NO fewer than 14 persons reportedly lost their lives in a road accident involving a DAF truck conveying 35 cattle and several passengers along Kontagora Road in Niger State. Zagazola Makama, a counter-insurgency publication, reported that the accident occurred around 11 a.m. on November 17 near Ibeto, as the truck, with registration number Lagos AZL 267 XH, travelled from Koko Local Government Area of Kebbi State to Lagos. “Police sources said an unidentified vehicle travelling in the same direction reportedly attempted to overtake the truck but brushed against it, causing the driver to lose control before the vehicle fell,” Makama said. “The truck driver and 13 other occupants reportedly died at the scene. “Those identified among the deceased included Umar, 45, the driver, from Kaoje; Anas Suleiman, 25, and Sufiyanu Suleiman, 40, both from Koko; Salim Abu Dogo, 30; Abubakar Shehu, 45; Yahaya Abubakar, 30; and Manu, 35, all from Dankigari. “Others were Rufai Umar, 25, from Bagudo; Faruk Tudu Kaoje, 20, from Kaoje; Umar Abubakar, 30, from Saradosa; Salisu Idry, 35, from Bagodo; and Abubakar Alhaji, 25, from Kaoje.” Police sources told Makama that relatives identified the bodies, while those claimed by their families were released for burial in accordance with Islamic rites. The publication added that two unidentified bodies had been deposited at the mortuary of Kontagora General Hospital. “The vehicle allegedly involved in the overtaking manoeuvre was later traced to Kaboji in Magama Local Government Area and taken to the Area Command Office,” Makama said. “However, the driver of the vehicle reportedly fled and remains at large.” According to the publication, the Niger State Police Command said investigation was ongoing to establish the full circumstances of the accident and apprehend the fleeing driver. The post 14 killed as truck carrying passengers, cattle crashes in Niger appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG issues Executive Order to end open defecation by 2030
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — The Federal Government has unveiled a new Executive Order to accelerate Nigeria’s efforts to eliminate open defecation by 2030, with state and local governments urged to strengthen sanitation financing, accountability and community mobilisation. The Open Defecation Free Nigeria by 2030 and Other Related Matters Order, 2025, was unveiled on Thursday during the commemoration of World Toilet Day and the seventh anniversary of the Clean Nigeria campaign in Abuja. Vice President Kashim Shettima, represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Delivery and Coordination in the Office of the Vice President, Akubo Adegbe, described the Executive Order as a decisive step towards translating government commitments into measurable sanitation outcomes. Shettima said the order marked a transition from fragmented interventions to stronger coordination, measurable results and sustainable national progress. He disclosed that since the launch of the Clean Nigeria campaign in 2019, 185 of the country’s 774 local government areas had attained Open Defecation Free (ODF) status, while Jigawa and Katsina remained the only states certified as open defecation-free. While acknowledging the progress recorded, the Vice President said Nigeria still had considerable ground to cover, urging states yet to achieve ODF status to establish monthly and quarterly targets and make their progress publicly available. He also warned against a reversal of gains in communities already certified as open defecation-free, stressing the need for sustained monitoring and accountability to protect existing achievements. According to him, achieving the 2030 target would require sustainable financing, reliable data, stronger institutions, effective implementation and continuous behavioural change. Shettima called on state and local governments to take ownership of the campaign by allocating adequate resources and strengthening sanitation institutions. He also urged development partners, the private sector, traditional rulers, community leaders and civil society organisations to sustain their support for the initiative. The Vice President, who chairs the Steering Committee of the Clean Nigeria Project, reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to working with subnational governments, adding that the National Economic Council would also be deployed to advance and sustain the national sanitation agenda. Linking the campaign to this year’s World Toilet Day theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality”, Shettima highlighted the disproportionate burden poor sanitation places on women and girls. He said inadequate access to safe and private sanitation facilities undermined their health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities. He therefore called for inclusive policies and investments that address the sanitation needs of women, girls, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups. item.title: Raye Tops the 2027 Grammy Nominations With 11 Including Album of the Year
item.description: Raye singing on stage with her band and backing vocalists. Photo Credit: Raye/Instagram When the 2027 Grammy nominations dropped earlier this week, one name sat right at the top of the entire board: Raye . Out of every artist in the running for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, she has the highest Grammy nominations this year with 11 nods, putting her ahead of Rosalía on nine. If you have been watching her rise over the past few years, seeing her command this much spotlight on music’s biggest stage feels well earned, especially for readers following global talent with Ghanaian roots through her mother’s side of the family. Her reaction online captured just how surreal the moment felt, writing on Instagram: “WHAT IS HAPPENING WHAT IS HAPPENING 11 GRAMMY NOMINATIONS INCLUDING ALBUM OF THE YEAR MY HEARTTTTT CANNOT EVEN FATHOM, MY HEARTTTTTTTT ” before following up with a simple “can’t stop crying .” Raye at home with her parents following the 2027 Grammy nominations announcement. Photo Credit: Raye/Instagram In case you are still catching up on her story, Raye was born Rachel Keen in London to a Ghanaian-Swiss mother and an English father, and she has spent years building a reputation as a sharp songwriter, vocalist, and arranger who refuses to stay boxed into one sound. Many listeners first got to know her through chart-topping collaborations and pop hooks before she parted ways with her former major label to release music independently, taking full creative control of her catalogue and storytelling. That independent leap paid off massively—her album This Music May Contain Hope topped the UK chart in March 2026 and won the 2026 Mercury Prize in October, turning her into one of the most talked-about voices in music. Artwork for This Music May Contain Hope. Photo Credit: Raye/Instagram Her 11 nominations for 2027 stretch right across her artistry, from songwriting and performance to arrangement, visuals, and full-length projects. This Music May Contain Hope is competing in both Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album, while her hit “ WHERE IS MY HUSBAND! “—which reached UK No. 1 in January 2026—is up for Record of the Year, Song of the Year, and Best Pop Solo Performance. She also earned nods for “ Click Clack Symphony ” alongside Hans Zimmer in Best Pop Duo/Group Performance, Best Arrangement, Instrumental and Vocals, and Best Music Video, plus “ Life Boat ” in Best Dance Pop Recording, “ I Hate the Way I Look Today” in Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance, and a Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical nod. Raye holding a number one award following a year of UK chart milestones, including “WHERE IS MY HUSBAND!” hitting No. 1 in January 2026 and This Music May Contain Hope topping the UK chart in March 2026. Photo Credit: Raye/Instagram This is not her first time on the Grammy radar, though it is easily her biggest moment yet. Before this sweep, Raye had four prior Grammy nominations—taking her career total to 15—including Best New Artist, Songwriter

item.title: Shettima, Issoufou reflect on Buhari’s legacy at biography launch
item.description: ‎–Late ex-President demonstrated leadership defined by character, not power –VP ‎–As Issoufou urges balanced assessment of Buhari’s achievements, controversies ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — THE Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima and former President of Niger Republic, Mahamadou Issoufou, yesterday reflected on the legacy of the late former Nigerian leader, Muhammadu Buhari, describing his life and political career as an important chapter in Nigeria’s history that offers enduring lessons on leadership, character and public accountability. ‎ While Shettima said Buhari demonstrated that the true measure of leadership lies in personal character rather than the power and privileges of public office, Issoufou urged Nigerians to assess the former President’s legacy objectively, taking into account his achievements, decisions and controversies. ‎ ‎The two leaders spoke at the public presentation of “Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography”, a three-volume account of the former President’s life and political career, held at the Nigerian Army Conference Centre and Suites, Abuja. ‎ ‎The Vice President, who was represented by the Special Adviser to the President on General Duties, Office of the Vice President, Dr Aliyu Modibbo, said Buhari’s modest lifestyle, personal discipline and devotion to national service distinguished him from many political leaders. ‎ ‎Speaking on the theme, “The Life We Leave to History”, the Vice President recalled lessons from his personal relationship with the late President, particularly his indifference to material possessions and commitment to Nigeria. ‎ ‎”He taught me that the dignity of office depends upon the character of its occupant. He also taught me that a leader’s example continues to speak long after he is out of service,” Shettima said. ‎ ‎He described Buhari’s Spartan lifestyle as remarkable in a political environment where public office is sometimes pursued to satisfy private interests. ‎ ‎”His Spartan lifestyle distinguished him in a world where too many seek public office to satisfy private appetites. There was something arresting about a man who could command so much and desire so little,” he stated. ‎ ‎Shettima noted that Buhari’s political journey, spanning military leadership and democratic governance, attracted both extraordinary public affection and strong criticism over his policies and decisions. ‎ ‎He, however, said the former President’s enduring connection with millions of Nigerians reflected a distinctive leadership disposition that defied conventional political calculations. ‎ ‎Beyond the tribute, the Vice President described the biography as an important contribution to historical documentation, institutional memory and public accountability. ‎ ‎He urged serving public officials to preserve records of their decisions and explain the circumstances surrounding them, warning that failure to do so could leave future generations vulnerable to speculation and distorted accounts of national

item.title: Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense company, feds say
item.description: A Russian national has been indicted on suspicions he was a Russian spy who stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley company that was assisting Ukraine in its ongoing war with its eastern neighbor. Igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the company’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors said Wednesday . He also kept a list of home addresses of employees and a senior executive. At one point, prosecutors said, D’iu trailed an employee as she traveled home from Palo Alto to San Francisco. An affidavit filed in the case referred to the employee as FEMP1, short for female employee, and said the event left her “in a state of emotional distress.” Evasive and irregular turns “FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote. “D’IU followed FEMP1 through U-turns, illegal left turns, and ran a red light to stay with FEMP1 for nearly thirty miles. FEMP1 called 911 while driving and was instructed to drive directly to San Francisco Police Department (“SFPD”) Mission Station. Near SFPD Mission Station, FEMP1 flagged an SFPD patrol vehicle and reported the incident. D’IU left once FEMP1 made contact with the patrol vehicle.” Read full article Comments

item.title: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert
item.description: In October 2025, four Black high school students were sharing Cool Ranch Doritos after football practice, winding down and waiting for their rides home. It was then, in the lull of a moment any teen with after-school activities knows well, that the school’s AI gun detection system suddenly flagged one teen holding a bag of chips as a potential gunman. Within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat. They recognized the Doritos bag and canceled the alert, which notified not only other school officials but also the Baltimore County Police Department that no response was needed. The false alert could have ended there—before a traumatizing campus clash with police—but it didn’t. Read full article Comments

item.title: 2027: People Are Rejecting Tinubu, They Can Feel The Pain — Dele Momodu
item.description: A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Dele Momodu, says Nigerians are rejecting President Bola Tinubu because they are feeling the adverse impact of his administration’s economic policies. Momodu, who is the Deputy Director-General of Media and Communications of the ADC presidential campaign council, said the growing public discontent was a reflection of the hardship Nigerians have endured since the removal of the fuel subsidy. The former Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) presidential aspirant made the remarks on Thursday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today. A combo of Dele Momodu and President Bola Tinubu Momodu said the government should have carefully considered the advantages and disadvantages of the policy before implementing it. He likened the country’s economic situation to a patient who had been given an injection and remained in a coma for almost four years. “That’s what is happening in Nigeria. And that is why you can see that everywhere Tinubu goes now, he is being rejected by the people. The people are not stupid; they are rejecting him because they can feel the pain,” he said. ﻿ The publisher accused the President of insensitivity to Nigerians’ economic hardship, citing excessive government spending, inadequate funding of critical sectors and the burden of subsidy removal. “We’ve since discovered that this subsidy issue could have been better handled because, if you look at it, the people who are at fault are probably less than 1,000 people, and now you are punishing over 200 million Nigerians because of the sins of a few people. “If he were sharing in the pain of the people, he would not be doing what he is doing, donating one billion, doing a budget to individuals, a budget in trillions, more than what you are paying the military, more than what you are using to service the health sector, more than what you are spending on the education of our children,” Momodu said. Momodu accused the Tinubu administration of covertly reinstating fuel subsidies and dismissed positive economic assessments by the World Bank and IMF, arguing that they had not improved Nigerians’ living conditions. “The world is praising us; the World Bank is praising us; the IMF is saying we are doing well. Whenever the IMF or World Bank is interested in your case, then something is wrong. You can see clearly that everything you can say is not affecting our people positively. Nigerians are suffering, and that’s just the truth,” he said. Subsidy Removal, ‘Bamayi’ ﻿ Tinubu announced the removal of the fuel subsidy during his inauguration on May 29, 2023, citing its growing cost to government finances. Since that announcement, the policy, alongside the unification of the foreign exchange market, has contributed to higher petrol prices and increased living costs for Nigerians. item.title: Palo Alto Networks opens wallet for open-weight training biz
item.description: As AI has become a thorn in the side of the security industry, Palo Alto Networks (PAN) has reached an agreement to acquire Applied Compute, an AI model training platform. "We believe many of the major disruptions of the last few weeks, including outages across major enterprises and governments, were partially due to unintended consequences of patching and configuration changes, as IT teams simply cannot patch these vulnerabilities fast enough without compromising their production environments," said Nikesh Arora, chairman and CEO of PAN, during the company's fiscal Q1 2027 earnings call on Wednesday. "The second effect is the rise of AI-assisted cyberattacks." So in the spirit of "hair of the dog that bit me," PAN is ingesting Applied Compute to make open-weight AI more secure for corporate customers. The answer to insecurity brought on by AI is buying security with AI. In its announcement of the tie-up, PAN declares "the future of enterprise AI is hybrid, and that a large share of enterprises will run on open-source and open-weight models tuned to their own data, cost, and control needs." That view has been clouded a bit by Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang's fall from grace: Back in July, he came to the defense of open-weight models as a defense against the hegemony of purveyors of closed-weight commercial models like Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI. His resignation as CEO of Nvidia has led to worries that the open-weight ecosystem has lost some lobbying power at a time when the US is wary about the uptake of models made in China. Nonetheless, PAN clearly sees a future for open-weight models. "Every enterprise is going to run a mix of open and closed models, and every one of those models needs to be secured," said Nikesh Arora, chairman and CEO of PAN, in a statement. "Applied Compute has built the best post-training and inference platform we've seen, and its research team is exceptional." The company expects the $4.5 billion all-stock transaction to add more than $1 billion to the company's Next Generation Security business by FY 2029. Arora, on the company's earnings call, explained the pricey bet as recognition of the corporate desire to avoid vendor lock-in and to retain control of data. "We're already seeing the desire for sovereignty and control compel enterprises to adopt open-weight and open-source models," he said. "Early signs of that shift are clear, with open-weight models growing from under 5 percent of token traffic to more than 60 percent over the past year." Beyond the sticker price, PAN is ready to up its infrastructure ante. Arora said the biz expects to build infrastructure supporting more than 100 megawatts of inference capacity, a project that will take "a modest CapEx commitment of less than $3 billion through fiscal 2030." ®

item.title: No more asteroid landing: Engine trouble forces Japan's Hayabusa2 probe to change plans
item.description: null Japan's space agency has decided to switch destinations and objectives for the final act of its Hayabusa2 mission, due to the spacecraft suffering trouble with its ion thrusters. The veteran Hayabusa2 spacecraft launched back in 2014 to collect material from the asteroid Ryugu . Since delivering the samples to Earth in December 2020 via a reentry capsule, the main spacecraft has been conducting an extended mission of exploration and in July made a super-close flyby of the two-headed asteroid Torifune. But Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end. The spacecraft was scheduled to rendezvous with, and attempt to land on, the tiny, 36-foot-wide (11 meters) near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031, but trouble with the aging spacecraft's engines has forced a change of plan. But Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end. The spacecraft was scheduled to rendezvous with, and attempt to land on, the tiny, 36-foot-wide (11 meters) near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031, but trouble with the aging spacecraft's engines has forced a change of plan. The spacecraft will instead target 2015 BM510, another tiny asteroid. And there will be no landing: Hayabusa2 is scheduled to make a high-speed flyby of the near-Earth object in April 2028. The decision was announced at a Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) press conference on Tuesday (Nov. 17), a day after a Cabinet Office space policy subcommittee meeting. The final functioning thruster out of Hayabusa2's four ion engines suffered a malfunction in mid-August, according to JAXA officials, while a sensor detected unexpected erosion of the spacecraft's surface during its long voyage in space. "The deterioration of the onboard equipment ... is becoming increasingly evident," Japan Times quoted Yuya Mimasu, team leader of the extended mission, as saying. A size comparison between asteroid Ryugu, which was visited by Hayabusa2 in 2020, and its planned next target, 1998 KY26. The 2031 visit to 1998 KY26 is now off, however; Hayabusa2 will instead fly by a different small asteroid in 2028. (Image credit: ESO/M. Kornmesser. Asteroid models: T. Santana-Ros, JAXA/University of Aizu/Kobe University) Despite losing the opportunity to land on KY26, the Hayabusa2 mission has been a huge success for JAXA, and the new direction promises its own intrigues. Asteroid 2015 BM510 has already attracted interest; it's the primary target of a proposal for the European Space Agency 's mini-Fast mission series. Scientists describe the body as a D-type asteroid, meaning it's thought to be organic-rich and comet-like, and may have originated in the outer solar system. Around the same time as Hayabusa2 conducts its high-speed flyby in April 2028, JAXA is also scheduled to launch its next asteroid mission, Destiny+. The mission on New Glenn is designed to deploy satellites, each with computing capacity at roughly the scale of a data center rack, into Sun-synchronous orbit where they can receive nearly continuous solar energy. "Project Suncatcher is a long-term moonshot to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit," said Travis Beals, senior director of Project Suncatcher at Google, in the news release. "This dedicated launch with Blue Origin represents a crucial milestone on our roadmap as we expand the boundaries of what's possible for the future of compute." Read full article Comments
